fields.title: Brain Training: Exercise Your Mind
fields.description: Overview of the cognitive health brain training exercises
fields.content:
Train your brain with fun, challenging puzzles that build mental sharpness.

## Available Exercises

- **Sudoku** - Fill a 9x9 grid using logic and deduction
- **KenKen** - Combine math operations with Sudoku-style logic
- **Nonogram** - Solve clues to reveal a hidden picture
- **Word Ladder** - Transform one word into another, one letter at a time
- **Memory Matrix** - Test your memory by recalling highlighted cells

## Your Progress

The hub shows your stats for each exercise:
- **Completed** - Total puzzles solved
- **Streak** - Consecutive days played
- **Best Score** - Your top performance

## Tips

- Start with easier difficulties to learn the rules
- Try different exercises to work various cognitive skills
- Consistency matters more than difficulty - play a little each day
- Use the **Stats** page to track improvement over time

fields.title: Brain Training Stats: Track Your Progress
fields.description: Understanding your brain training statistics and improvement trends
fields.content:
See how your cognitive fitness is improving over time.

## What You'll See

- **Overall Stats** - Total sessions, time trained, current streak
- **Per-Exercise Stats** - Performance breakdown for each game
- **Improvement Trends** - How your scores and times are changing

## Key Metrics

- **Completion Rate** - What percentage of started puzzles you finish
- **Average Score** - Your typical performance level
- **Best Score** - Your peak performance
- **Streak** - Consecutive days with at least one completed exercise

## Tips

- Focus on consistency rather than perfection
- Compare yourself to your own past performance, not others
- A longer streak builds stronger neural pathways

fields.title: How to Play Sudoku
fields.description: Rules and tips for solving Sudoku puzzles
fields.content:
Fill the 9x9 grid so every row, column, and 3x3 box contains the digits 1-9 exactly once.

## Rules

1. Each **row** must contain 1-9 with no repeats
2. Each **column** must contain 1-9 with no repeats
3. Each **3x3 box** must contain 1-9 with no repeats
4. Pre-filled numbers (darker cells) cannot be changed

## Controls

- **Click** a cell to select it
- **Number keys (1-9)** or tap the number pad to enter a digit
- **Delete/Backspace** to erase a cell
- **Arrow keys** to move between cells
- **N key** to toggle Notes mode

## Notes Mode

Press **N** or tap the **Notes** button to enter pencil marks:
- Small numbers appear in the corner of the cell
- Track possible values for each cell
- Notes auto-clear when you enter a final answer

## Tips

- Look for rows/columns/boxes missing only 1-2 numbers
- Use **notes** to track possibilities, then eliminate
- Red numbers mean a conflict - same digit appears twice in a row, column, or box
- **Undo** (Ctrl+Z) lets you back up if you get stuck
- The number pad shows how many of each digit are placed

fields.title: How to Play KenKen
fields.description: Rules and tips for solving KenKen puzzles
fields.content:
KenKen combines Sudoku logic with arithmetic. Fill the grid so each row and column has unique numbers, and each cage meets its math target.

## Rules

1. Fill the grid with numbers **1 to N** (where N = grid size: 4, 5, or 6)
2. Each **row** must contain each number exactly once
3. Each **column** must contain each number exactly once
4. Each **cage** (outlined group of cells) has a target number and operation
5. The numbers in a cage must combine using that operation to equal the target

## Cage Operations

- **+ (Addition):** Numbers add up to the target. Example: "8+" means cells sum to 8
- **− (Subtraction):** Difference equals the target (2-cell cages only)
- **× (Multiplication):** Product equals the target. Example: "12×" means cells multiply to 12
- **÷ (Division):** Quotient equals the target (2-cell cages only)
- **No operation:** Single-cell cage, the number IS the target

## Controls

- **Click** a cell to select it
- **Number keys** or tap the number pad to enter a value
- **Delete/Backspace** to clear a cell

## Tips

- Start with **single-cell cages** - the answer is given!
- Look for cages where only one combination of numbers works
- Remember: in a 4x4 grid, only use numbers 1-4
- Think about both constraints: the cage math AND row/column uniqueness
- Subtraction and division cages only have 2 cells, making them easier to solve first

fields.title: How to Play Nonogram
fields.description: Rules and tips for solving Nonogram picture puzzles
fields.content:
Nonograms are picture logic puzzles. Use the number clues to figure out which cells to fill, revealing a hidden image.

## Rules

1. **Row clues** (left side) tell you which cells are filled in that row
2. **Column clues** (top) tell you which cells are filled in that column
3. Each number = a group of consecutive filled cells
4. Groups must appear in order, separated by **at least one empty cell**
5. Example: "3 2" means 3 filled cells, a gap, then 2 filled cells

## Controls

- **Fill Tool** (default): Click or drag to fill cells black
- **Mark Tool**: Click or drag to mark cells with X (known empty)
- Toggle between tools using the buttons at the top
- Drag across multiple cells to fill/mark a whole row quickly

## Grid Sizes

- **Easy:** 5x5
- **Medium:** 10x10
- **Hard:** 15x15

## Tips

- Start with the **largest clue numbers** - they have fewer possible positions
- If a clue equals the row/column size, fill the entire row/column
- **Mark empty cells** with X to keep track of what you've figured out
- Look for **overlapping** possibilities - cells that must be filled regardless of position
- Work from the edges inward
- Grid lines every 5 cells help you count spaces accurately

fields.title: How to Play Word Ladder
fields.description: Rules and tips for solving Word Ladder puzzles
fields.content:
Transform the start word into the end word by changing **one letter at a time**. Every step must be a valid English word.

## Rules

1. The **start word** (blue) and **end word** (green) are given
2. Change exactly **one letter** per step
3. Every intermediate word must be a **real English word**
4. All words are the same length

## Example

CAT → COT → COG → DOG

## Controls

- Click the **+** button to add a new step
- Type letters using the keyboard or on-screen buttons
- Letters auto-advance to the next position
- **Delete/Backspace** to go back and fix mistakes

## Visual Feedback

- **Green border** = valid step (exactly 1 letter different from previous word)
- **Red border** = invalid step (0 or 2+ letters different)

## Tips

- Think about which letters need to change between start and end
- Change **vowels** first - they often have more valid word options
- If stuck, try working **backwards** from the end word
- Fewer steps = better score
- Common short words (3-4 letters) have many valid neighbors

fields.title: How to Play Memory Matrix
fields.description: Rules and tips for the Memory Matrix exercise
fields.content:
Test and strengthen your visual memory. Memorize which cells are highlighted, then select them from a blank grid.

## How It Works

### Phase 1: Get Ready
A countdown prepares you to focus.

### Phase 2: Memorize
The grid appears with certain cells **highlighted**. Study their positions carefully - you have a few seconds.

### Phase 3: Recall
The grid goes blank. **Click the cells** you remember being highlighted. A counter shows how many you've selected vs. how many to find.

### Phase 4: Results
- **Green** = correctly selected
- **Red** = incorrectly selected (wasn't highlighted)
- **Yellow** = missed (was highlighted but you didn't select it)

## Grid Sizes

- **Easy:** 3x3 (fewer cells to remember)
- **Medium:** 4x4
- **Hard:** 5x5
- **Expert:** 6x6

## Tips

- **Chunk** the cells into groups or patterns (L-shape, diagonal, etc.)
- Use the grid edges as reference points
- Look for **symmetry** in the highlighted pattern
- Don't overthink - your first instinct is often right
- Practice regularly to expand your working memory capacity
